summary: arXiv:2611.23244v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Goemans conjectured that any fractional single-source flow could be converted into an unsplittable flow without increasing total cost and while increasing any arc load by at most the largest demand. title: Response-Relevant Information Is Not Sufficient for Neural Training-State Equivalence
summary: arXiv:2611.23245v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Response-relevant information is not sufficient evidence that two neural networks are in the same training state. We define training-state equivalence operationally: two checkpoints are equivalent, relative to an intervention family and horizon, if they respond alike when training is perturbed and continues.

summary: arXiv:2611.23246v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Nearly all current methods for computing reachable sets of nonlinear dynamics propagate them with truncated Taylor expansions plus rigorous remainders. The expansion is pointwise: once its argument is a whole set rather than a point, one polynomial must stay accurate across that set, and it reaches only as far as its disc of convergence.

title: Budgeted Proper Loss Design for Uncertain Decision Thresholds
summary: arXiv:2611.23247v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A binary probability estimate may be used by several decision makers with different error costs. Proper scoring rules can emphasize selected probability thresholds, but a single average threshold distribution need not give a good worst-case regret guarantee.

title: Exploring Parkinson's Diagnosis Using Machine Learning Techniques
summary: arXiv:2611.23248v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In recent years, machine learning (ML) techniques have emerged as promising tools for accurate and timely diagnosis of Parkinson's disease (PD) which is an incurable neurodegenerative disorder. summary: arXiv:2611.23339v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Generative recommendation (GR) inference differs substantially from conventional LLM serving, featuring long input sequences, wide beam search, and only a few fixed output tokens. summary: arXiv:2611.23342v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The rapid development of materials machine learning relies on large-scale, heterogeneous datasets, yet model reliability is often compromised by imperfect data from diverse experiments, simulations, and database integration. title: When Does Subspace Direction Matter for LoRA? Regime Analysis of the Magnitude Principle in Few-Shot Adaptation
summary: arXiv:2611.23428v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that the importance of a LoRA adapter's initial input-subspace direction is regime-dependent, and we characterize this dependence in theory and experiment. This refines the recent view that spectral initializers help through update magnitude alone.

title: Conformally Calibrated Adaptive Computation in Neural Operators
summary: arXiv:2611.23440v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Selecting less computation in a neural operator need not reduce inference time. We study this gap using conformal calibration to choose Fourier modes or channel width per input subject to a fixed error budget.

summary: arXiv:2611.23463v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Speculative decoding accelerates language-model generation by verifying multiple draft tokens in a single target-model pass. However, better draft predictions and longer accepted continuations do not necessarily produce faster generation.

A leading published machine-learning targeting system excluded 53 per cent of eligible households as deployed.

title: Stability of Parallel Transport Convolution under Riemannian Metric Perturbations
summary: arXiv:2611.23543v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Geometric convolutions on Riemannian manifolds depend on the geometry of the underlying domain, making stability under metric perturbations a fundamental question in geometric deep learning. This paper studies this question for parallel transport convolution through methods from differential geometry and analysis.

title: Safe to Omit, Worth Omitting? Keeping the Answer and Cutting Latency When an LLM Agent Skips Another's Message
summary: arXiv:2611.23570v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In multi-agent systems, a receiver agent often waits for a helper agent's message (text or its latent KV cache), which can improve performance but adds latency. We study when a receiver agent can skip the message safely (the final answer rarely changes) and beneficially (the time saved exceeds the cost of deciding).

summary: arXiv:2611.23596v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study variance-dependent reinforcement learning in episodic time-inhomogeneous linear Markov decision processes (MDPs) with feature dimension $d$, horizon $H$, and $K$ episodes. title: DuoCL: Dual-Path Online Continual Learning
summary: arXiv:2611.23598v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Online continual learning (OCL) requires learning from a data stream whose arrival rate is independent of model training speed. When training cannot keep pace, computationally expensive gradient-based methods update less frequently, limiting adaptation.

summary: arXiv:2611.23600v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Path-based attribution methods like Integrated Gradients (IG) are widely used to interpret neural networks, yet imperceptible input perturbations can drastically alter their attribution maps while leaving model predictions unchanged. title: FairPGT: Partitioned Graph Transformers for Dual-Level Fair Graph Clustering
summary: arXiv:2611.23631v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Clustering on attributed graphs can produce demographically biased clusters, particularly when communities align with protected groups. Graph transformers can amplify this bias through same-group attention, while global attention limits scalability.

title: Toaster: Nonlinear Memory from Cascaded Linear Memories and Target Propagation
summary: arXiv:2611.23648v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recurrent memories let language models process long sequences with a fixed-size state. Linear memories such as DeltaNet and KDA store one matrix and take one delta-rule step per token.

title: Learning through Discernment: when a small language model learns from user feedback on the job, and when it decays
summary: arXiv:2611.23716v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Small language models on devices could keep improving by learning, overnight, from their own daily work. summary: arXiv:2611.23718v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Scientific experiments continually reveal prediction errors. Effective updates depend on which parameters change and which errors drive the correction.

summary: arXiv:2611.23403v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents achieve state-of-the-art performance across domains through chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning. title: Language Models Make New Research Sound Old
summary: arXiv:2611.23546v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Researchers are increasingly using large language models (LLMs) to validate research questions. We find that LLMs make open research questions sound partly studied and overstate what related papers establish.

title: PFN-Syn: Generating Synthetic Tabular Data with Prior-Data Fitted Networks
summary: arXiv:2611.28440v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Synthetic tabular data can help enable data sharing and model development in privacy-sensitive domains, but existing generators often require dataset-specific training and substantial computation. A request to send a file to an approved recipient can look harmless even when that file was assembled, several steps earlier, from data the user said must never leave.

title: HiPPO Functional Memory: Coordinate-Queryable Attention for Irregular Time Series
summary: arXiv:2611.28465v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Irregular time series are recorded at nonuniform times and are often queried at other times: between observations, after the last one, or on a regular grid. Continuous-time models answer such queries by integrating latent dynamics, and time-aware attention models answer them by revisiting the observation tokens.

summary: arXiv:2611.28476v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Zeroth-order (ZO) optimization provides a computationally efficient approach to fine-tuning large language models (LLMs), but conventional methods typically rely on isotropic perturbations that ignore the anisotropic structure of neural-network parameter spaces. summary: arXiv:2611.28488v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Outlier detection is often deployed in fully unsupervised settings, where labels are unavailable and practitioners must choose a detector without direct performance feedback. title: State of Mind: Learning and Evaluating World Models of Naturalistic Brain Dynamics
summary: arXiv:2611.28508v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Understanding naturalistic brain activity requires going beyond the stimulus alone, as external inputs continuously interact with an individual's evolving brain state. A world model captures such dynamics in a latent state by inferring it from neural observations, predicting stimulus-driven evolution, and updating with new observations.

title: DisSparse: Pipelined Top-$p$ Sparse Attention for Long-Context LLM Serving
summary: arXiv:2611.28522v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Long-context LLM inference is bottlenecked by the memory demands of the key-value (KV) cache, whose size scales linearly with context length. Dynamic sparse attention reduces this bottleneck by fetching and attending only to a critical subset of tokens.

summary: arXiv:2611.28582v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Self-rewarding optimization (SRO) promises to improve language models by enabling them to generate their own reward signals. Yet when and how SRO succeeds or fails remains poorly understood.

summary: arXiv:2611.28595v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Memory-efficient Muon methods aim to reduce storage overhead while preserving strong performance, yet existing approaches compromise either convergence guarantees or practical efficiency. summary: arXiv:2611.28603v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Knowledge distillation transfers capabilities from large language models to smaller students, yet stronger teachers do not always yield better students. Recent studies report diminishing or even negative returns from teacher scaling.

title: BitShare: Sensitivity-Aware Binning and Bit Sharing for Compacting LLM Weight Storage
summary: arXiv:2611.28607v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Decoding with large language models at small batch sizes is limited by memory bandwidth, so the bits stored per weight largely set its cost. Group-wise integer quantization stores every weight of a group at the same precision, although the input channels of a group differ in sensitivity.

summary: arXiv:2611.28611v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reinforcement-learning agents shape the observations they encounter; consequently, detecting out-of-distribution (OOD) states requires analysing action-conditioned trajectories rather than treating inputs as independent samples. title: Interpreting Diffusion Model Activations in Natural Language
summary: arXiv:2611.28621v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Interpreting the intermediate activations of diffusion models (DMs) is key to understanding how they generate images. title: Nearly Minimax-Optimal Sample Complexity of Natural Policy Gradient with a Matching Information-Theoretic Lower Bound
summary: arXiv:2611.28628v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A fundamental question in reinforcement learning is how many sampled transitions are needed to learn a near-optimal policy, and whether direct policy optimization can attain this statistical limit. title: What Counts as Attack Success? Evaluating Harmfulness in Red Teaming LLMs
summary: arXiv:2611.28038v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Judging whether a model response is harmful requires contextual and normative choices, yet red-teaming studies often delegate this judgment to automated evaluators. We examine how harmfulness criteria are specified in red-teaming research and how they carry through to reported results.

title: Distributionally-Verifiable Rewards for Human-Behavior Simulation
summary: arXiv:2611.28048v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models are increasingly used to simulate survey respondents in social-science research. A useful simulator should predict individual responses, reproduce population response distributions, and capture demographic differences.

title: Benchmarking and Adapting LLMs for English-Swedish Medical Question Answering
summary: arXiv:2611.28050v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models do well on English medical exams, but less is known about Swedish. This matters most for small open models that hospitals can run locally.

title: SnakeTranslate: Weakly Supervised Policy Learning from Offline Parallel Text for Simultaneous Translation
summary: arXiv:2611.28055v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Adaptive simultaneous translation requires reliable prefix translation and timely READ/WRITE decisions, but ordinary parallel corpora provide no action annotations. We present SnakeTranslate, which adapts loss-derived alignment to sampled causal histories for jointly learning both capabilities.

summary: arXiv:2611.28298v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Modern language models (LMs) are post-trained and deployed as agents inside a "harness", but standard harness designs accumulate context that the neural network is forced to generalize to, making training for long-horizon tasks expensive and time-consuming. summary: arXiv:2611.28349v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Under structured outputs (JSON schemas, regexes, tool calls), speculative drafters do not see the grammar constraint and repeatedly propose invalid keys, delimiters, and indentation, while the grammar engine already knows which tokens must come next. title: Contrastive On-Policy Distillation via Dual-Branch Supervision
summary: arXiv:2611.28359v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For on-policy distillation (OPD), more capable models are a natural choice as teachers. However, higher task performance does not necessarily imply greater teachability.

summary: arXiv:2611.28374v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Enterprise agents must maintain an up-to-date understanding of work distributed across heterogeneous artifacts, evolving over time, and unevenly visible to different collaborators. We formulate this challenge as persistent project-state understanding (PPSU) and introduce PULSE, a benchmark of 1,573 questions over 30 enterprise project histories.

summary: arXiv:2611.28383v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models are increasingly used to construct synthetic publics. Prior work has documented errors in individual responses, population heterogeneity, and prompt robustness, but whether these failures reflect a common loss of fidelity or distinct properties of synthetic populations remains unclear.

title: Digital Knockoffs
summary: arXiv:2611.28482v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Social simulations often use language model agents to represent people who differ on several measurable traits. However, describing a trait profile in a prompt does not guarantee the agent will express each trait at its intended level.

title: Digital Twins for Multi-Agent Systems: When to Trust, What to Change
summary: arXiv:2611.28517v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Digital twins of agent networks need to flag unreliable forecasts and help users choose interventions. summary: arXiv:2611.28525v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A risky choice can be described by what will be saved or what will be lost, and people often choose differently depending on that wording. summary: arXiv:2611.28542v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Production text-to-code systems use large language models to turn natural-language analytics requests into executable SQL and pandas code. Existing benchmarks cover both tasks but do not isolate when performance diverges between them.

title: Tool-to-Self: Internalizing Visual Tool Capabilities via Scaffolded Reinforcement Learning

title: Modeling Perceived Promptness in Simultaneous Interpreting from Quality, Structure, and Timing Signals
